summary: Priority-aware HTTP request orchestration for mobile/offline-sensitive scenarios, often paired with punchclock.
recommendedPatterns: Use Fusillade when request prioritization or deduplication is a real product requirement.
Pair it with Akavache when offline cache behavior matters.
avoidPatterns: Do not add Fusillade for trivial API access.
Do not hide prioritization rules in scattered call sites.
setupSteps: Define priority-aware HTTP clients or handlers.
Integrate with caching only when justified.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting that Fusillade policy should be visible at the composition root.

packageSelection: Use Fusillade.Reactive only when full System.Reactive compatibility is required.
Compose it under Refit/HttpClient handlers rather than duplicating network policy in API clients.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Use Refit's generated clients as the primary typed API surface and place Fusillade handlers underneath them.
Use ReactiveUI.SourceGenerators for command/state boilerplate around network operations.
compatibilityNotes: The lean and .Reactive packages share the scheduling design but expose different reactive interop types.
Only safe/idempotent HTTP methods are candidates for duplicate request coalescing.
migrationGuidance: Move System.Reactive-facing Fusillade consumers to the lean package and Primitives types by default.
Keep Fusillade.Reactive at an explicit boundary when Unit/IScheduler/Rx public contracts must be preserved.

harvest.sourceSummary: Official upstream main-branch README and current NuGet package metadata.
